3. The necessary facts for disposal of the Rule are that the 'Ka Schedule' land appertained to SA khatian No. 232 and some other SA khatians under mouza-Damurtala and 'Kha Schedule' land appertained to SA khatian No. 242 and some other SA khatians under mouza-Raghunathpur, Thana and District Narail and 'Ga Schedule' movable property belonged to Zitu Beg, husband of the plaintiff Hazera Begum. Zitu Beg had no issue and he sold some of his land to one Md Shahidul Islam. As he became older and older and ill, he appointed the plaintiff as his attorney by registered deed of irrevocable power of attorney dated 17-9-1990 for his property and delivered possession thereof. The plaintiff took possession of the suit land and during her possession, on 26-1-1991 corresponding to 12 Magh 1398 BS Zitu Beg died. Thereafter, on 7 Poush 1398 BS, the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 claimed title over the suit land as heirs of Zitu Beg denying the title of the plaintiff thereto. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are not heirs of Zitu Beg. Koresh Beg was the father of Zitu Beg and Koresh Beg had brothers and sisters. As the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 denied the title of the plaintiffs to the suit land, her title thereto had been clouded and as such, she filed the suit for declaration of her title to the suit land. 

 8. I have perused the revision petition and the LCR. It appears that in the Ka and Kha Schedules of the plaint, CS plot numbers have been mentioned without mentioning the CS khatian numbers. Instead, SA khatian numbers have been mentioned. It appears that the plaintiffs did not file any of the SA khatians. It further appears that the plaintiff filed CS khatian No. 584 and other CS khatians, Exhibit 2 series. Exhibit 2 CS khatian No. 101 shows that the land of this khatian belonged to Abdul Wazed Beg and others. It appears from Exhibit 2(ka) CS khatian No. 422 that the land of this. khatian belonged to Naimuddin Beg and others. Exhibit 2 (kha) CS khatian No. 170 shows that the land of this khatian belonged to Wazed Beg. Koresh Beg and others It is evident from Exhibit 2(g) CS khatian No. 584 that the land of this khatian belonged to Surja kanta Ghosh. The plaintiff did not mention the CS khatians in the plaint though CS plots have been mentioned in the schedules. It appears that the defendant also did not file any SA khatian but they filed CS khatian No. 222, Exhibit Ga which shows that the land of this khatian belonged to Ismail Beg and Abdul Beg. 

 9. It may be mentioned that no statements about CS as well as SA record have been made in the body of the plaint. The genealogy of the CS recorded tenants has not been mentioned in the plaint. Though both the parties have claimed that Zitu Beg was the owner of the suit land, but in fact neither party stated in the pleading the mode of acquisition of title of Zitu Beg right from CS record. It ought to have been stated in the respective pleading of the parties since they have filed CS khatians and it has been mentioned in the written statement that Zitu Beg owned the suit land by purchase and inheritance. It is not understood as to how the learned Advocate for the plaintiff drafted the plaint without narrating the mode of acquisition of title of Zitu Beg in the suit land. It is also not understood as to how the Courts below passed their judgments without perusal of the SA khatians and discussing about CS khatians and mode of acquisition of title of Zitu Beg in the suit land, particularly when Koresh Beg, father of Zitu Beg is the CS recorded tenant vide Exhibit 2(Kha) and thus, I find that both the Courts below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in their judgments and decrees. In fact, they ought to have instructed the plaintiff to amend the plaint by narrating the mode of acquisition of title of Zitu Beg in the suit land in view of the CS khatians as filed by her. Therefore, the impugned judgment and decree and those of the trial Court have no foundation and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree cannot stand.
